learning: Iteration 6 showed the simulator is deterministic for a fixed design, so single-race comparisons on this geometry are reliable. The s-bend and slalom max_error limit (about 0.064 m against a 0.06 m off-track limit) is not moved by mass, track or sensor size changes tested so far. Any further gain has to come from controller changes tested in a later iteration, or from a forward sensor offset that the Builder has not yet tested.
notes: Controller and geometry are both identical to the iteration 1 reference, so this package isolates repeatability. Any change in outcome from 324 would indicate a problem in the integration rather than a design effect.
rationale: The Builder's geometry is the iteration 1 design, which is also the iteration 6 repeat. Iteration 6 reproduced iteration 1 exactly (score 324.0661, oval finish 0.70, same per-track metrics), so the simulator is deterministic for this design and controller. That makes iteration 1 the reference for judging any change. Every other tested change lowered the score: 16 mm sensors (159.26), wheel_track 0.10 m with kp 4.5 (175.19), mass 0.6 kg (247.82) and mass 0.7 kg (185.49). I therefore keep the controller identical to iteration 1 (kp 5.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.6, base_speed 1.2, line_loss last_direction, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1]). Changing gains now would be untested on the stable base, and iteration 2 showed that changing several settings at once can confound the result. The s-bend and slalom max_error sits at about 0.064 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit. Neither geometry nor the untested controller changes I have evidence for address that, so this race is mainly a repeatability check of the reference. The expected result is about 324, with an oval finish rate near 0.70.
